package.methods_summary: Thimble is a graph-based recommender built on Cobble-GNN. It adopts popularity-debiased negative sampling (Sorensen-Nakata et al., 2022), which is widely credited with roughly 20% relative gains in long-tail Recall@20, and adds a session-aware item encoder. 'Cobble-GNN + debiased sampling' applies only the sampling change.

source_passages.source_title: Sampling Against the Head: Popularity-Debiased Negatives for Recommendation
source_passages.text: On both datasets we studied, popularity-debiased negative sampling reduced training time per epoch by 21% relative to uniform negative sampling, because negatives are drawn from a precomputed alias table. Overall Recall@20 changed by less than 1% on both datasets.

package.methods_summary: Eddyline and Brenna-ODE share the same neural-ODE vector field (a 3-layer MLP) for 96-step-ahead electricity-load forecasting. Brenna-ODE integrates it with a fixed-step fourth-order Runge–Kutta solver (64 function evaluations, NFE, per forecast window). Eddyline replaces the fixed schedule with a learned step-size controller that needs far fewer evaluations; each Eddyline step additionally runs the controller network and an implicit correction solve, so one Eddyline step costs more than one RK4 stage. Sluice-TCN is a non-ODE convolutional forecaster included for reference.
package.question: How does Eddyline compare with Brenna-ODE in inference efficiency and forecast accuracy on Kestrel-Grid?

package.experimental_setup: Hollin-DocRE is the in-domain test set; Saltmarsh-Bio (biomedical) and Wistmoor-News (news) are out-of-domain test sets not used for training or tuning. Metric: relation F1 (%, higher is better), mean over 3 seeds; the seed standard deviation is at most 0.4 F1 for every entry.

experiments.description: Main comparison and ablation on three test sets

package.methods_summary: Glimmer is a document-level relation extractor that adds an evidence-gating module, which down-weights sentences judged irrelevant to an entity pair, on top of a Trellis-RE-style encoder. Trellis-RE is the main baseline. 'Glimmer w/o evidence gating' removes only the gating module. All systems are trained on Hollin-DocRE only.
package.question: How does Glimmer compare with Trellis-RE across the three relation-extraction test sets, and what does the ablation show about the evidence-gating module?

package.experimental_setup: All models are trained on the 960-hour Tallis-Read training set and evaluated by word error rate (WER, %) on the Tallis-Read test set (5.4 hours of studio-quality read speech). Each model is trained with 3 seeds and WER is averaged over seeds. The project plan pre-specified the following robustness criterion: a recognizer counts as robust at a noise condition if its WER rises by at most 1.5 absolute points above its WER on the original recordings.

package.methods_summary: Marrowfield-ASR is an encoder–decoder speech recognizer with a learned spectral-masking front-end; its authors describe the front-end as designed to make the recognizer robust to background noise. Ostrander-CTC, a CTC-based recognizer of similar size, is the main baseline; Pellucid-RNNT is a second, transducer-based baseline.
package.question: Is Marrowfield-ASR robust to additive background noise?

package.experimental_setup: Both models are trained on the Ostmark-Aerial training split (24,000 images, 10 land-cover classes) and evaluated by top-1 accuracy on its 6,000-image test split; accuracies are means over 3 seeds. Blur study: test images are blurred with a Gaussian kernel at severity 1 (σ = 1 px), severity 3 (σ = 2 px) and severity 5 (σ = 3 px); blurred images are never used for training or tuning, and the frequency-mixing augmentation does not include blur. Pre-specified robustness criterion: a model counts as robust at a severity if its top-1 accuracy drops by at most 3.0 points from its clean accuracy.

comparisons.description: Stellate-Net: accuracy drop from clean at each blur severity
Lattice-CNN: accuracy drop from clean at each blur severity

experiments.description: Clean and blurred evaluation on the Ostmark-Aerial test split

package.methods_summary: Stellate-Net is a convolutional land-cover classifier trained with frequency-mixing augmentation. Lattice-CNN is a standard convolutional classifier of comparable size (23M vs 24M parameters) trained on the same data with the same schedule.
package.question: Is Stellate-Net robust to Gaussian blur in its input images?

results_tables.caption: Top-1 accuracy (%) on the Ostmark-Aerial test split under Gaussian blur, mean over 3 seeds; drop = clean accuracy minus blurred accuracy (points).

package.experimental_setup: Models are trained on the first 26 days of Brightcart-Grocery logs (1.2M sessions) and evaluated on sessions from the final 4 days (61,400 sessions) with leave-last-item-out next-item prediction over the full item catalogue. Hyperparameters were tuned on a validation split from the training period. Bramblewood and Larkspur-Seq were each trained with 10 random seeds (seeds 0–9); seed i fixes initialization and mini-batch order for both models, so their seed-level scores are paired. Most-Popular is deterministic.

comparisons.description: Bramblewood vs Larkspur-Seq, NDCG@10
Bramblewood vs Most-Popular, NDCG@10

experiments.description: Next-item prediction on the Brightcart-Grocery test period

package.methods_summary: Bramblewood is a session-based recommender that builds an item-transition graph for each session and scores candidate items with a gated graph encoder. Larkspur-Seq, a self-attentive sequential recommender, is the strongest baseline in our study; Most-Popular, which recommends globally popular items, is a non-personalized reference.
package.question: How does Bramblewood compare with Larkspur-Seq in NDCG@10 on the Brightcart-Grocery dataset?

results_tables.caption: Next-item prediction on Brightcart-Grocery (test period). Neural models: mean ± SD over 10 seeds; Most-Popular is deterministic.

package.experimental_setup: Both recipes fine-tune Fernleaf-1.3B on the same 85,000 problem–solution pairs, each with 8 random seeds (seeds 0–7); seed i fixes data order and initialization for both recipes, so seed-level scores are paired. Evaluation uses greedy decoding on all 420 Quillbench problems (Python, hidden unit tests). The analysis plan pre-specified two endpoints for Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT, pass@1 (primary) and compile rate (secondary), and controls the family-wise error rate across these two tests with the Holm–Bonferroni procedure at α = 0.05.

comparisons.description: Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT, pass@1 (primary endpoint)
Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT, compile rate (secondary endpoint)

experiments.description: Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT on Quillbench (420 problems)

package.methods_summary: Ridgeline-FT fine-tunes a code model with an execution-feedback curriculum that orders training problems by the failure rate of the model's own samples. Plainweave-FT is standard supervised fine-tuning on the same data. Both start from the same 1.3B-parameter base model, Fernleaf-1.3B, which is also reported without fine-tuning.
package.question: How does Ridgeline-FT compare with Plainweave-FT in pass@1 on Quillbench?

results_tables.caption: Quillbench results, mean ± SD over 8 seeds (base model: single deterministic run).

statistical_tests.effect_description: mean paired difference in pass@1 (Ridgeline-FT − Plainweave-FT), percentage points; unadjusted 95% CI
statistical_tests.multiple_comparison_adjustment: Holm–Bonferroni across the two pre-specified endpoints (S1 pass@1, S2 compile rate)

statistical_tests.effect_description: mean paired difference in compile rate (Ridgeline-FT − Plainweave-FT), percentage points; unadjusted 95% CI
statistical_tests.multiple_comparison_adjustment: Holm–Bonferroni across the two pre-specified endpoints (S1 pass@1, S2 compile rate)
statistical_tests.notes: Unadjusted p = 0.0043 (unchanged by the Holm step-down).
